doc.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019

title: Not transcribing, and Dizzy versus Miles at the Village Gate
summary: Longo rejects learning by transcribing and compares Miles and Dizzy when he played behind both at the Village Gate.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Well said. I wanted to read something about you from the three volume Grove Dictionary of Jazz, which you’re in. And this person, whoever wrote this, he says, “Mike’s style as a pianist is based on those of Oscar Peterson and Bud Powell, to which he has added a personal and contemplative approach.”

Well I play like me. You see I never did any of that transcribing. First of all transcribing to me is the greatest ear training in the world but you can not learn to play from transcribing, which is a big mistake they’re making in the jazz ed departments. Because that’s not you. You’re playing somebody else’s — they say well that’s vocabulary. That’s not the way people learn vocabulary. When you’re a child you learn a vocabulary. Apple. Give me the apple. You take the apple. You don’t learn — you don’t repeat a conversation you heard your parents — and so transcribing and playing the transcription is something I don’t agree with because you will never get your own — and you can’t swing that way man because you’re not playing you. You’re not playing your own rhythms. And so it takes longer to develop something that way. That’s why if you listen to Miles on the early records with Bird, he don’t sound that good. It took a while for him. But he was going for his own sound. He wasn’t trying to copy Dizzy. First of all he couldn’t. And I played with both of them at the same time at the Village Gate with Dizzy and Miles. And I would play behind both of them. And I could see a big difference
between the two players. Miles, he sounded great with his group, but when he played with us, a little funny.
He didn’t have those kind of chops.
No. He couldn’t play up along at the time where Dizzy was.
Where Dizzy was playing in real time and also his improvisations would stand up to analysis like a composed piece.
